text:
Left: what the model gave me. Right: what went on air.

The gap between those two frames is the actual job.

This carousel is the full assembly line for one Jai Hanuman episode, in the order I run it. Slide 9 is where most of the hours go, and it isn't generation.

Save it if you're building AI video in Indian languages. Which step would you automate first?
slides: Step 1. Story check. Every scene against Valmiki and Tulsidas. Devotional audiences notice everything.
Step 2. Character bible. One locked 3D style, asset tags for every character and prop, a master list of camera angles.
Step 3. Storyboard prompts, then shots in Seedance 2.0. Vertical 9:16 from the first frame, never cropped later.
Step 4. Dialect dialogue. Not translation. Idioms, taunts and jokes change from boli to boli.
Step 5. Voices in ElevenLabs v3 with emotion tags on every line. Music in Suno.
Step 6. Edit. Episodes run 5 to 8 minutes. Two went out every Saturday.
Step 7. A promo cut for each region. A promo editor's instinct still decides the first 3 seconds.
The hardest part: keeping Hanuman ji's face and proportions identical across hundreds of shots. The style lock and asset tags from Step 2 are what made it possible.
Built on STAGE's in-house AI tool, made by our tech team. The audience cares about one thing: hearing its own boli.
media_brief: Export as a 10-page PDF, 1080x1350. Slide 1 = before/after split frame. One step per slide, large type, one supporting frame each.
